To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Thursday launch handover for Inês

DRAFT — for me to review on the train before sharing.

Inês,

I’m sorry to leave you with this, especially with a correction to sort out two days before the launch. My father is ill, I am with my family. I don’t yet know how long I’ll be away, so please plan to lead Thursday without me.

I trust you completely. You know this paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself. You do not need to deliver my version of the presentation or wait for me to approve every decision. Make it yours. The priorities are to get the number corrected everywhere, get the revised arrangements agreed with the host’s office, and give yourself enough space to prepare.

You can call me. After 09:00 tomorrow, Tuesday, I might not pick up; please don’t let that hold things up. Geert knows I’m away and can sign off the corrected press release if Hanna needs a senior name.

1. First: get the correction moving with Hanna

The correct estimate for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion.

Figure 3 and the summary had the number from the old run, which did not apply the free allocation phase-out. I found this this afternoon. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does. We need to be direct about that rather than describe it as a cosmetic correction.

What is already done:
- PDF v7 on the drive is corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. Use that version.

What is not done:
- Deck v4 still needs correcting on slides 6 and 9. Slide 9 contains the revenue chart.
- The embargoed press release Hanna sent on Friday still says EUR 2.1 billion.

Please contact Hanna first and ask her to arrange a corrected release and an explicit correction to all 34 Brussels contacts who received the original. The embargo lifts Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET. This needs to reach them before then, ideally well before Wednesday’s background calls. Ask her to make clear which release and PDF supersede the earlier material, and to confirm when the correction has gone out.

A line she can use, subject to checking the final wording:

“The estimate for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The earlier figure came from a model run that did not apply the free allocation phase-out. This changes the headline revenue estimate but not the paper’s conclusion. Please use the corrected release and PDF v7.”

If she needs senior approval, go to Geert rather than waiting for me.

The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. If anyone asks, you should say so plainly: “That was Marieke’s error; the corrected estimate is EUR 1.4 billion.” You do not have to absorb responsibility for it because you are the person standing at the lectern.

2. Next: correct the deck and make one clean launch set

Please update slides 6 and 9 against PDF v7, including the chart and any labels that carry the old number. Check the speaker notes too: you left mine in, and I don’t want an old figure hiding there after the visible slides are fixed. A quick search for “2.1” across the deck and any launch copy we intend to use would be sensible.

Save the corrected deck as a clearly identified new version so nobody accidentally presents v4. Use the corrected PDF and deck for the press calls and the event. Please ask Hanna to check that anything she has queued for publication also uses EUR 1.4 billion and PDF v7.

There are 14 slides in the current deck, but the presentation now needs to be 15 minutes, not 20. Cut whatever you need to. I would rather you have a clear, comfortable presentation with time to explain the corrected estimate than race through all my notes.

3. Confirm the revised event arrangements with Tomás

The run of show in the folder is out of date. Tomás emailed today: Lindqvist has a vote and must leave at 13:30. He has asked for the presentation to be shortened to 15 minutes and the panel to begin at 12:50. She wants to take at least two questions herself before leaving.

Please tell Tomás you will replace me for both the presentation and the panel, and confirm the revised timings with him. Ask him to agree when those questions will happen and who will moderate after Lindqvist leaves. Don’t assume the original 13:40 Q&A slot deals with her request.

The working schedule, pending that confirmation, is:
- 12:00: guests at the security entrance; badges collected by Tomás. Light lunch outside the room from 12:00.
- 12:30: Lindqvist’s welcome, five minutes.
- 12:35: your presentation, 15 minutes.
- 12:50: panel with you, Dr. Abena Owusu-Mensah and Florian Kessler.
- Before 13:30: at least two questions with Lindqvist, with the exact slot to be agreed.
- 13:30: Lindqvist leaves; moderation arrangements need confirming.
- 14:00: close.

The venue is the European Parliament, Altiero Spinelli building, in the room booked by Lindqvist’s office.

The hard administrative deadline is Wednesday 25 November at 12:00: Tomás needs final names of everyone attending from our side. Please make sure your name and anyone supporting you are on that list. He was explicit that security will not admit people whose names are missing.

4. Wednesday: press calls and a final practical check

Hanna promised two journalists a Wednesday afternoon background call: one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. The calendar has 14:00 and 15:00 on Wednesday 25 November, 20 minutes each by phone, but these are still marked “Hanna to confirm”.

Please ask Hanna to confirm the times and contacts and tell them you will take the calls instead of me. If the timings don’t work alongside preparation, arrange an alternative with her rather than trying to do everything at once. Both journalists should have the correction before speaking with you.

Abena’s remote link is in the calendar invite. Your deck note says she tested it successfully, so there is no need to start from scratch, but please let her know you are taking over and arrange a short sound/link check before the event. Confirm who in the room will handle the connection.

5. For the panel: acknowledge the challenge, then keep the discussion on the paper

Kessler has already said he will challenge the 80% downstream steel-cost pass-through assumption and raise resource shuffling. Be ready for both, but don’t let him make the whole event a referendum on the central-case assumption.

On pass-through, the honest answer is:
- 80% is the central case, not a claim that every small manufacturer can pass through that amount.
- Annex B tests 40% and 60%.
- The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%.

Say that openly. Don’t imply the result is equally strong at every level. You ran those sensitivities; you can explain what they do and do not establish better than anyone. Then bring the discussion back to what the findings mean for LDCs and the revenue choices the paper is addressing.

On resource shuffling, acknowledge the risk. We cover it in section 5.2 and recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. There is no need to defend a position we haven’t taken.

Abena was strong on the LDC implications on our call. Make room for her perspective, but don’t count on her to answer Kessler for us.

And please remember Lisbon. When the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel without making it look like a rescue. You are better live than you think. You don’t need my speaker notes to do this well.

6. Before the room fills, arrange the small follow-up jobs

Lucy Tran from Halvorsen is attending with a colleague. For the grant report she needs two event photos and attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please assign someone to take the photos and record attendance before the event begins, so neither task lands on you while you’re presenting. Afterwards, make sure those reach Lucy by that date if possible.

The things that must not slip are the press correction before the embargo lifts, the badge list by Wednesday noon, and a corrected deck ready for Thursday. Delegate the rest where you can.

I’m sorry about the error and about handing you the repair work just as I leave. You have my full trust to lead this, including changing the plan where it needs changing. Please don’t wait for a reply from me to make a sensible call.

Marieke
